NASHR:v2p310/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p310/r1.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v2p310/r1.claim: The chapter refers back to Hafs's previously discussed brief pause on ʿiwajā.
NASHR:v2p310/r1.anchor: تقدم سكت حفص على عوجا في بابه

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r5.claim: The shift from direct address in the preceding sura to ‘His servant’ honors the Prophet through possessive attribution; the wording does not say ‘sent down upon you.’
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r5.anchor: والتفت من الخطاب في قوله وكبره تكبيرا إلى الغيبة في قوله على عبده

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r6.claim: One explanation says qayyiman confirms that the book is perfectly straight, an interpretation also attributed to al-Ḍaḥḥāk.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r6.anchor: وقيما تأكيد لإثبات الاستقامة إن كان مدلوله مستقيما وهو قول ابن عباس والضحاك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r7.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r7.claim: Other explanations make the Quran upright in people’s welfare, religious laws, and worldly and afterlife affairs, or an authority that confirms prior books.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p134/r7.anchor: وقيل: قيما بمصالح العباد وشرائع دينهم وأمور معاشهم ومعادهم

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r1.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r1.claim: Al-Zamakhsharī coordinates the negated clause with ‘sent down,’ placing it inside the relative clause; then qayyiman is governed by an omitted verb to avoid separating a circumstantial from its owner.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r1.anchor: فزعم الزمخشري أنها معطوفة على أنزل فهي داخلة في الصلة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r2.speaker: ابن عطية
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAṭiyya makes qayyiman a circumstantial of the book, semantically advanced, with the negation interposed; alternatively an omitted verb governs it.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r2.anchor: وقال ابن عطية: قيما نصب على الحال من الكتاب فهو بمعنى التقديم مؤخر في اللفظ

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r3.speaker: العسكري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r3.claim: Al-ʿAskarī proposes fronting and postponement: praise God for the upright Quran without crookedness, since eloquence puts the most important point first.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r3.anchor: وقال العسكري: في الآية تقديم وتأخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r4.speaker: أبو عبد الله الرازي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r4.claim: Al-Rāzī says ‘no crookedness’ establishes the Quran’s perfection in itself and ‘upright’ its perfection for others; he rejects the proposed inversion as rationally impossible.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r4.anchor: وقال أبو عبد الله الرازي: ولم يجعل له عوجا يدل على كونه مكملا في ذاته

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r5.speaker: الكرماني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r5.claim: Al-Kirmānī says the apparent analysis has two circumstantials of one book: first a clause, then a single word, without any inversion.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r5.anchor: وقال الكرماني: إذا جعلته حالا وهو الأظهر فليس فيه تقديم ولا تأخير

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r6.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r6.speaker: الأصبهاني
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r6.claim: Al-Aṣbahānī favors two sequential circumstantials, meaning the book was made neither crooked nor anything but upright.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r6.anchor: واختاره الأصبهاني وقال: هما حالان متواليان والتقدير غير جاعل له عوجا قيما

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r7.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r7.speaker: صاحب حل العقد
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r7.claim: The author of Ḥall al-ʿIqd allows qayyiman as a single-word substitute for the entire negated clause; he notes a grammatical dispute over such substitution.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r7.anchor: وقال صاحب حل العقد: يمكن أن يكون قوله قيما بدلا من قوله ولم يجعل له عوجا

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r8.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r8.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r8.claim: Qayyiman may instead describe the attached pronoun in lahu as either a stable or temporary state; the pronoun apparently refers to the book, though some refer it to the Prophet.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r8.anchor: والظاهر أن الضمير في له عائد على الكتاب وعليه التخاريج الإعرابية السابقة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r9.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r9.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r9.claim: Ḥafṣ pauses lightly after ʿiwajan before qayyiman; a Companion codex’s added ‘but made it upright’ is a gloss, not a Quranic reading.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v7p135/r9.anchor: وحفص يسكت على قوله عوجا سكتة خفيفة ثم يقول قيما

ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r8.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r8.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r8.claim: In the esoteric reading, the station of servitude is unmatched, and the Prophet reaches its highest rank as the true servant, free of both worlds.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p257/r8.anchor: قد تقدم أن مقام العبودية لا يشابهه مقام ولا يدانيه ونبينا صلى الله عليه وسلم في أعلى مراقيه

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r3.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r3.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r3.claim: The surah begins with praise so the second half of the Qur'an opens with الحمد لله, echoing the opening of the first half in al-Fātiḥa and the approximate start of the fourth quarter in Q 35:1.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r3.anchor: وهي مفتتحة بالحمد حتى يكون افتتاح النصف الثاني من القرآن ب الحمد لله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r4.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r4.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r4.claim: Its opening praises God for revealing the Book, exalts the Qur'an against polytheists and their People-of-the-Book informants, warns those who ascribe a child to God, and promises believers reward.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r4.anchor: افتتحت بالتحميد على إنزال الكتاب للتنويه بالقرآن تطاولا من الله تعالى على المشركين

IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r5.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r5.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r5.claim: The introduction comforts the Prophet over the pause in revelation, then criticizes attachment to worldly adornment and turns to the story of the Cave youths.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v15p244/r5.anchor: وتسلية رسول الله عن أقوالهم حين تريث الوحي لما اقتضته سنة الله مع أوليائه

ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.claim: The surah's parables contrast faith in God with undue attachment to worldly life; its key idea is that earthly beauty tests people, most clearly in the rich and poor men story.
ASAD-NOTES:18:intro/r1.anchor: and the key-phrase of the whole surah is the statement in verse 7,

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.claim: Al-Kahf is late Makkan, although a minority consider its first eight verses Madinan.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r1.anchor: is a late Makkan sūrah, although a minority hold

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r2.speaker: Reports in the source
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r2.claim: Reports say reciting the first and last ten verses protects against the trials of the grave or al-Dajjāl, the Antichrist figure Christ defeats at the end of time.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r2.anchor: Several reports indicate that reciting the first and last ten verses of this sūrah has the power to protect one

STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r4.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r4.claim: Warnings of judgment and punishment connect the narratives; the close evokes God's inexhaustible Word and reminds that the Prophet is human and receives revelation.
STUDYQURAN:18:intro/r4.anchor: The sūrah closes by evoking the inexhaustibility of God’s Word

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The sūrah begins with the same subject as the preceding sūrah’s conclusion.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: This sūrah begins with the same topic on which the previous sūrah ended

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Arabs owe gratitude for the Qur’an, but instead some fail to value this favour and invent excuses to deny it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: show gratitude and not otherwise. Unfortunate are the people who are not valuing this favour

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Qur’an is free of ambiguity in text and meaning, lucid Arabic, and guides to the straight path through arguments found in human nature, intellect and the world.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: It guides people to the straight path

BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r1.claim: Muhammad is the perfect servant, free of all besides God; his concern for his community on Judgment Day contrasts with other prophets' concern for themselves, and rejects Christian claims about Jesus.
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r1.anchor: محمد الذي يستأهل أن يكون عبدا مطلقا حقيقيا حرا عن جميع ما سوى الله

BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r2.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r2.claim: The Qur'an is truly a “book,” linguistically a joining of letters; praising its revelation highlights it as one of God's greatest gifts and the means to both worlds' felicity.
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r2.anchor: القرآن الحقيق باسم الكتاب وهو في اللغة جمع الحروف ورتب استحقاق الحمد على إنزاله

BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r3.claim: The Qur'an has no crookedness: no disorder in composition, contradiction of meaning, or departure from truth toward falsehood.
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r3.anchor: شيئا من العوج بنوع اختلال في النظم وتناف في المعنى أو عدول عن الحق إلى الباطل

BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r4.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r4.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r4.claim: Hafs from ʿAsim pauses briefly without breathing at ʿiwajā to prevent the next word being mistaken for its description, and also pauses at marqadnā to avoid a bad break or misleading connection.
BURSEVI:v5p166#2/r4.anchor: واختار حفص عن عاصم السكت على عوجا وهو وقفة لطيفة من غير تنفس

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r1.claim: The surah is also called “The Companions of the Cave,” according to a report collected by Ibn Mardawayh; an Ibn Abbas report says the Torah calls it “the barrier,” protecting its reciter from fire, but al-Bayhaqi grades that report munkar.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r1.anchor: ويقال سورة أصحاب الكهف كما في حديث أخرجه ابن مردويه وروى البيهقي من حديث ابن عباس مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r2.claim: The majority say the whole surah is Meccan, a view chosen by al-Dani and transmitted from Ibn Abbas and Ibn al-Zubayr; a report from Anas says it descended all at once with seventy thousand angels.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r2.anchor: وهي مكية كلها في المشهور واختاره الداني وروي عن ابن عباس وابن الزبير

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.speaker: مقاتل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.claim: Muqatil says the surah is Meccan except its opening through “barren ground” (18:8) and the passage beginning “Indeed, those who believe” through the end.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r4.anchor: وقال مقاتل : هي مكية إلا أولها إلى ( جرزا ) وقوله تعالى : ( إن الذين آمنوا ) إلى آخرها فمدني

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r5.claim: Regional verse counts differ: Basrans count 111, Kufans 110, Syrians 106, and Hijazis 105.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r5.anchor: وهي مائة وإحدى عشرة آية عند البصريين ومائة وعشرة عند الكوفيين ومائة وست عند الشاميين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r6.claim: One coherence argument is that the preceding surah opens with glorification and this one with praise, paired on the scales and repeatedly joined in expressions such as “glorify with praise”; their endings and beginnings also correspond.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r6.anchor: افتتاح تلك بالتسبيح وهذه بالتحميد وهما مقترنان في الميزان وسائر الكلام نحو ( فسبح بحمد ربك

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r7.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r7.claim: A further comparison distinguishes the preceding surah's final praise as essential praise and this surah's opening praise as indicating deservedness other than by essence.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r7.anchor: فرق بينهما بأن الحمد الأول ظاهر الحمد الذاتي والحمد المفتتح به في هذه يدل على الإستحقاق الغير الذاتي

ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r12.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r12.speaker: ابن عمر
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r12.claim: A report from Ibn Umar says that reciting the Cave on Friday brings light from beneath one's feet to the sky until the Resurrection and forgives the sins between Fridays.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p199/r12.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن ابن عمر مرفوعا

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r1.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r1.claim: Several transmitters report from Abu Said al-Khudri that Friday recitation of the Cave lights the distance between its reader and the Sacred House.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r1.anchor: وروى غير واحد عن أبي سعيد الخدري من قرأ سورة الكهف في يوم الجمعة أضاء له من النور

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r2.speaker: الحسن بن علي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r2.claim: Umm Musa reports that al-Hasan ibn Ali used to recite the surah every night.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r2.anchor: كما أخرج أبو عبيد والبيهقي عن أم موسى يقرأها كل ليلة

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r3.speaker: عبد الله بن مغفل
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r3.claim: A report from Abd Allah ibn Mughaffal says Satan does not enter that night a house where the Cave is recited.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r3.anchor: أخرج ابن مردويه عن عبد الله بن مغفل مرفوعا البيت الذي تقرأ فيه سورة الكهف لا يدخله الشيطان

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r4.claim: Several imams recommend reciting the surah on Friday and its eve, and repeating the recitation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r4.anchor: وإلى سنية قراءتها يوم الجمعة وكذا ليلتها ذهب غير واحد من الأئمة وقالوا بندب تكرار قراءتها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r5.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r5.claim: A report from Abu al-Darda says memorizing the first ten verses protects against the Dajjal's trial; another version says to recite the final ten.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r5.anchor: من حفظ عشر آيات من أول سورة الكهف عصم من فتنة الدجال

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r6.speaker: أبو الدرداء
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r6.claim: A further report, authenticated by al-Tirmidhi, says reciting three verses from the beginning of the Cave protects from the Dajjal's trial.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r6.anchor: وأخرج الترمذي وصححه عنه مرفوعا من قرأ ثلاث آيات من أول الكهف عصم

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r7.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r7.speaker: عائشة
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r7.claim: A report attributed to Aisha says whoever recites the final five verses before sleep is raised by God at whichever hour of the night He wills; the author says he tried it repeatedly.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200/r7.anchor: مرفوعا إن من قرأ الخمس الأواخر منها عند نومه

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r1.claim: The “Book” is the complete Qur'an, self-sufficient in perfection and uniquely deserving the name, or the revelation already sent at that point; the relative clause explains why God deserves praise and magnifies the revelation.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r1.anchor: الكتاب ( الكامل الغني عن الوصف بالكمال المعروف بذلك من بين سائر الكتب الحقيق باختصاص اسم الكتاب به

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r2.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant honors both messenger and revelation and indicates that a messenger must be the sender's servant, unlike Christian claims about Jesus.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r2.anchor: بالعبد مضافا إلى ضميره تعالى من الإشارة إلى تعظيمه عليه الصلاة والسلام

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r3.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r3.claim: The direct object “Book” is delayed after the prepositional phrase so that “and He made no crookedness in it” can immediately follow it.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r3.anchor: وتأخير المفعول الصريح عن الجار والمجرور مع أن حقه التقديم عليه ليتصل به قوله تعالى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r4.claim: The denied crookedness includes defects of grammatical wording or eloquence, contradiction in meaning, falsehood, or calling to other than God.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r4.anchor: أي شيئا من العوج باختلال اللفظ من جهة الإعراب ومخالفة الفصاحة وتناقض المعنى

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r5.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r5.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r5.claim: A lexical distinction assigns kasra in ʿiwaj to inward or intelligible deviation and fatha in ʿawaj to physical deviation visible to the eye.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r5.anchor: هو بكسر العين ما يدرك بفتح العين وبفتح العين ما يدرك بفتح العين

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r6.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r6.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r6.claim: The distinction is challenged because the earth in 20:107 is physical; one answer says the verse denies subtle unevenness detectable only by geometry and insight, though “you do not see” seems to describe sight; Ibn al-Sikkit says the kasra form is broader.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#2/r6.anchor: وأورد عليه قوله تعالى في شأن الأرض ( لا ترى فيها عوجا ولا أمتا ) فإن الأرض محسوسة واعوجاجها

ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#3/r1.speaker: المرزوقي
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#3/r1.claim: Al-Marzuki, in his commentary on al-Fasih, chooses that the kasra and fatha forms of ʿiwaj/ʿawaj have no difference in meaning.
ALUSI-FULL:v15p200#3/r1.anchor: واختار المرزوقي في شرح الفصيح أنه لا فرق بينهما

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r1.claim: God praises Himself for blessing creation with the Book, singling out His Messenger because its revelation was a special blessing for him and a general one for everyone.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r1.anchor: أثنى الله (1) على نفسه بإنعامه على خلقه وخص رسوله صلى الله عليه وسلم بالذكر

BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r6.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r6.speaker: قيل
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r6.claim: Another view says the Qur'an is uncreated, citing Ibn Abbas's gloss on 39:28, a Qur'an in Arabic without ʿiwaj.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v5p141#2/r6.anchor: وقيل: معناه لم يجعله مخلوقا وروي عن ابن عباس في قوله: "قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج"

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r1.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r1.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r1.claim: The Qur’an is the greatest divine favor because it guides people to perfection and to what orders worldly and afterlife welfare.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r1.anchor: رتب استحقاق الحمد على إنزاله تنبيها على أنه أعظم نعمائه

BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r2.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r2.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r2.claim: It has no flaw in wording, contradiction in meaning, or deviation from truth; semantic crookedness parallels crookedness in physical things.
BAYDAWI-FULL:18:1/r2.anchor: اختلال في اللفظ وتناف في المعنى

QASHANI:18:1/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:1/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:1/r1.claim: In praising God for the book's descent, He praises Himself in differentiated form from the perspective of unity: He is both praiser and praised in unity and detail.
QASHANI:18:1/r1.anchor: أثنى الله تعالى بلسان التفصيل على نفسه باعتبار الجمع من حيث كونه منعوتا بإنزال الكتاب

QASHANI:18:1/r2.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:1/r2.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:1/r2.claim: The Prophet was eternally singled out as God's servant and prepared to receive the complete book; descent unfolds unified realities in his human manifestation, while his ascent returns their meaning as praise.
QASHANI:18:1/r2.anchor: قابلة للكمال المطلق من فيضه وإيداع كتاب الجمع فيه بالقوة

QASHANI:18:1/r3.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:1/r3.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:1/r3.claim: God first praised Himself in unity through differentiation, then said Praise belongs to God; the Prophet's praise depends on God's prior disclosure, as expressed in the transmitted prayer.
QASHANI:18:1/r3.anchor: لا أحصي ثناء عليك أنت كما أثنيت على نفسك

QASHANI:18:1-2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Qāshānī
QASHANI:18:1-2/r1.speaker: author
QASHANI:18:1-2/r1.claim: The book has no crookedness, meaning no deviation toward another; the Prophet's sight saw no other in witnessing.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r3.claim: Where the prior surah ends with the Prophet praising God as free of defects, this one begins by declaring God's worthiness of praise for His perfection and for the wise religion conveyed through the unrivaled upright book.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r3.anchor: بدئت هذه بالإخبار باستحقاقه سبحانه الحمد

BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r4.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r4.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r4.claim: The opening teaches servants how to praise God in wording suited to the occasion; praise encompasses the attributes of perfection and belongs to Him intrinsically.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r4.anchor: معلما لهم كيف يثنون عليه , مفقها لهم في اختلاف العبارات باختلاف المقامات

BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r5.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r5.claim: God deserves praise both in Himself and for His attributes and acts.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p441#2/r5.anchor: أخبر بأنه يستحقه أيضا لصفاته وأفعاله

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r1.claim: The Qur'an gathers the meanings of previous scriptures; Moses' Torah commands justice in rulings, while David's Psalms call toward renunciation and benevolence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r1.anchor: كما آتى موسى التوراة الآمرة بالعدل في الأحكام , وداود الزبور الحادي إلى الزهد والإحسان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r2.claim: Calling Muhammad God's servant before mentioning the book honors him, points to the Night Journey, and authenticates his mission without needing Quraysh to consult Jews; the book gathers the meanings of earlier scriptures such as the Torah and Psalms.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r2.anchor: مقدما له على المنزل لأن المراد الدلالة على صحة رسالته بما لا يحتاج فيه قريش

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r3.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r3.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r3.claim: God says He made no crookedness 'for' the book, denying even the possibility of distortion because its comprehensive revelation is from the Knower of the unseen; ʿiwaj with kasra denotes meanings, while fatḥa denotes physical things.

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r5.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r5.speaker: سعد الدين التفتازاني
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r5.claim: Al-Taftāzānī says surahs opening with praise point to one of four foundational blessings: initial creation and preservation, then a second creation and preservation; al-Fātiḥa signals all four and al-Anʿām the first creation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r5.anchor: أن كل سورة افتتحت بالحمد فللإشارة إلى نعمة من أمهات النعم

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r6.claim: Al-Kahf points to the first preservation: the world's order and human continuity depend on prophets and scripture.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r6.anchor: فإن نظام العالم وبقاء النوع الإنساني يكون بالنبي والكتاب

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r8.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r8.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r8.claim: The four praise-opened surahs map human history: pre-accountability learning and covenant, the life of moral responsibility warned by earlier peoples' ruin, the intermediate state awaiting resurrection, and eventual second creation and preservation.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r8.anchor: وكأن سن الاحتلام كان أول الإيجاد من الإعدام

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r9.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r9.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r9.claim: The interval from al-Fātiḥa to al-Anʿām signifies childhood's preparation in scripture, monotheism, religious community, and law; puberty marks life emerging from nonexistence.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r9.anchor: إلا في تعلم الكتاب والتوحيد والاجتماع على أهل الدين

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r10.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r10.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r10.claim: Surahs from al-Anʿām to al-Kahf recall earlier peoples' destruction as warnings for the accountable lifespan; al-Kahf's closing praise with monotheism urges ending life with the highest religious virtues.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r10.anchor: وأشير إلى بقية العمر وهو زمان التكليف بما بين الأنعام وهذه السورة

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r11.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r11.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r11.claim: The interval from al-Kahf toward the surah of second creation represents the barzakh, where ties end, all creatures gather, divine power is disclosed, and the two groups settle permanently in paradise or hell.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r11.anchor: وأشير إلى مهلة البرزخ بما بين هذه وسورة الإيجاد الثاني

BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r12.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r12.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r12.claim: Surahs from al-Kahf through Saba emphasize resurrection more than earlier surahs, with some opening on it and building their discourse upon it.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p442/r12.anchor: وأكثر فيما بين هذه وبين سبأ من أمر البعث كثرة ليست فيما مضى

BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.claim: The stories reproach Israelites for delaying faith and presuming their answers to Quraysh made them uniquely knowledgeable; Moses and Khidr's story calls them to submit to God's encompassing knowledge.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r1.anchor: وفي كل ذلك من تأديب بني إسرائيل وتقريعهم وتوبيخ مرتكبهم في توقفهم عن الإيمان

BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r2.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r2.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r2.claim: The spirit question was joined to the Night Journey in al-Isra because both concern the hidden realm; the Quran, the spirit that orders existence, is greater than the spirit they asked about.
BIQAI-FULL:v4p445/r2.anchor: أن الروح ضمت إليها , لأنه من سر الملكوت كالإسراء

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.claim: Ḥafṣ from ʿĀṣim pauses slightly after ʿiwajā and after marqadnā in 36:52.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r1.anchor: كان حفص عن عاصم يسكت عند قوله عوجا سكتة خفيفة

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.claim: When revelation resumed, opening praise of God for sending the Book rebuked Quraysh, who wished him ill but saw blessing on him.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r3.anchor: فافتتح الوحي بحمد الله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.claim: The Book is the Qur'an; “no crookedness” means it was not diverted from the upright course.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r4.anchor: والكتاب هو القرآن، وقوله ولم يجعل له عوجا أي لم يزله

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r5.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r5.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r5.claim: In Arabic ʿiwaj with kasra describes abstractions and roads; ʿawaj with fatḥa describes physical things like sticks and walls.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r5.anchor: وهو بكسر العين في الأمور والطرق وما لا يحس متنصبا

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r6.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r6.speaker: ابن عباس
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r6.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās glosses the phrase as meaning the Qur'an was not created.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v3p494#2/r6.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: معناه ولم يجعله مخلوقا

SULAMI:v1p400/r1.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r1.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p400/r1.claim: The verse attributes everything wholly to God and describes the servant as sincere, owning nothing.
SULAMI:v1p400/r1.anchor: سمعت ابن عطاء يقول في قوله : ﴿ الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ﴾ ، قال : أضاف الكل بالكلية إلى نفسه

SULAMI:v1p400/r2.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r2.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p400/r2.claim: One definition of the servant is a person who sees no one besides the master.
SULAMI:v1p400/r2.anchor: وقيل : العبد الذي لا يرى غير سيده

SULAMI:v1p400/r3.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r3.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p400/r3.claim: Another definition is a person who disputes nothing with the master.
SULAMI:v1p400/r3.anchor: وقيل : العبد الذي لا ينازع سيده شيئا

SULAMI:v1p400/r4.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r4.speaker: author
SULAMI:v1p400/r4.claim: Another definition is a person who cares for, settles into, or feels secure about nothing.
SULAMI:v1p400/r4.anchor: وقيل العبد الذي لا يهتم بشيء ولا يسكن إلى شيء ، ولا يأمن من شيء

SULAMI:v1p400/r5.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r5.speaker: أبو حفص
SULAMI:v1p400/r5.claim: The servant eagerly stands ready to fulfill the master's commands, having been made the locus of his command.
SULAMI:v1p400/r5.anchor: قال أبو حفص : العبد القائم إلى أوامر سيده على حد النشاط حديث جعله محل أمره

SULAMI:v1p400/r6.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r6.speaker: أبو عثمان
SULAMI:v1p400/r6.claim: The servant owns nothing and takes no care of anything for himself.
SULAMI:v1p400/r6.anchor: وقال أبو عثمان : العبد الذي لا يملك شيئا ولا يرعى لنفسه شيئا

SULAMI:v1p400/r7.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r7.speaker: الجريري
SULAMI:v1p400/r7.claim: True servanthood means taking on the master's character traits.
SULAMI:v1p400/r7.anchor: وقال الجريري : حقيقة العبد هو المتخلق بأخلاق سيده

SULAMI:v1p400/r8.author: al-Sulamī
SULAMI:v1p400/r8.speaker: ابن عطاء
SULAMI:v1p400/r8.claim: The revealed scripture is manifest and contains its inner secrets.
SULAMI:v1p400/r8.anchor: وقال ابن عطاء : الكتاب منشور ظاهر فيه أسرار باطنه

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r1.speaker: author
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r1.claim: The author refers the explanation of praise to al-Fatiha; the servant is Muhammad and the Book is the Quran, whose revelation benefits the Prophet especially and all people generally.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r1.anchor: قد شرحناه في أول الفاتحة والمراد بعبده هاهنا محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم وبالكتاب القرآن

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r2.speaker: العلماء باللغة والتفسير
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r2.claim: Linguists and exegetes say the verse has fronting and postponement, with the reconstructed order: He sent the Book down upon His servant.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v5p103/r2.anchor: قال العلماء باللغة والتفسير في هذه الآية تقديم وتأخير تقديرها أنزل على عبده الكتاب

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r1.claim: God praises Himself at the openings and endings of matters and is worthy of praise in every state, in this life and the next.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r1.anchor: قد تقدم في أول التفسير أنه تعالى يحمد نفسه المقدسة عند (1) فواتح الأمور وخواتيمها، فإنه المحمود على كل حال،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r2.claim: Revelation of the noble Book to Muhammad is God’s greatest blessing on earth’s people because it brings them from darkness into light and guides them on a clear, straight path.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r2.anchor: ولهذا حمد نفسه على إنزاله كتابه العزيز على رسوله الكريم محمد، صلوات الله وسلامه عليه؛ فإنه أعظم نعمة (2) أنعمها الله على أهل الأرض؛ إذ أخرجهم به من الظلمات إلى النور،

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r3.claim: The Book has no deviation, crookedness, or turning aside; it is upright, a clear warning to unbelievers and glad news to believers.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v5p135#2/r3.anchor: حيث جعله كتابا مستقيما لا اعوجاج فيه ولا زيغ، بل يهدي إلى صراط مستقيم، بينا واضحا جليا (3) نذيرا للكافرين وبشيرا للمؤمنين؛

JISHUMI:v6p4338/r4.author: al-Ḥākim al-Jishumī
JISHUMI:v6p4338/r4.speaker: author
JISHUMI:v6p4338/r4.claim: With fatḥa, عوج describes visible crookedness; with kasra it describes imperceptible matters such as religion or speech.
JISHUMI:v6p4338/r4.anchor: العوج بالفتح: فيما يرى كالقناة والخشبة، وبالكسر فيما لا يرى كالدين والكلام.

AKHFASH:v2p427/r1.author: al-Akhfash al-Awsaṭ
AKHFASH:v2p427/r1.speaker: author
AKHFASH:v2p427/r1.claim: قيما describes the revealed Book: God sent down the Book as upright and without crookedness.
AKHFASH:v2p427/r1.anchor: قال {عوجا} {قيما} أي: أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا.

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p655#2/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p655#2/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p655#2/r4.claim: The surah is Meccan except verse 38 and verses 83–101, which are Medinan; it has 110 verses and followed al-Ghāshiya in revelation.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p655#2/r4.anchor:
مكية ( إلا آية 38 ومن آية 83 إلى غاية آية 101 فمدنية )
وآياتها 110 ( نزلت بعد الغاشية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r1.claim: God teaches His servants to praise Him for Islam, their greatest blessing, and the Book revealed to Muhammad that brings salvation and success.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r1.anchor: لقن الله عباده وفقههم كيف يثنون عليه ويحمدونه على أجزل نعمائه عليهم وهي نعمة الإسلام

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r2.claim: God made the Book wholly free of crookedness; for meanings, crookedness means contradiction or anything departing from wisdom and correctness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r2.anchor: ولم يجعل له شيئا من العوج قط ، والعوج في المعاني كالعوج في الأعيان ، والمراد نفي الاختلاف والتناقض عن معانيه

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r3.claim: Qayyiman is best parsed with an implied verb rather than as a circumstantial modifier, avoiding separation from its noun by part of the relative clause; absence of crookedness thereby establishes uprightness.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r3.anchor: الأحسن أن ينتصب بمضمر ولا يجعل حالا من الكتاب ؛ لأن قوله { ولم يجعل } معطوف على أنزل ، فهو داخل في حيز الصلة

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r4.claim: Pairing the denial of crookedness with the assertion of uprightness emphasizes perfection, since an apparently straight thing might still show subtle defects under close inspection.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r4.anchor: فائدته التأكيد ، فرب مستقيم مشهود له بالاستقامة ولا يخلو من أدنى عوج عند السبر والتصفح

KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r5.claim: Other readings of qayyiman make the Book a confirmer and witness of other scriptures, or one that directs people's interests and necessary laws.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v2p657/r5.anchor: وقيل : قيما على سائر الكتب مصدقا لها ، شاهدا بصحتها . وقيل : قيما بمصالح العباد

FARRA:v2p133#2/r1.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v2p133#2/r1.speaker: author
FARRA:v2p133#2/r1.claim: قيما modifies the revealed Book: God praised Himself for sending a straight, sustaining scripture without crookedness; قيم on books means that it verifies them.
FARRA:v2p133#2/r1.anchor: قوله تبارك وتعالى: ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما المعنى: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما، ولم يجعل له عوجا.

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.claim: God praises Himself for revealing the Quran to His servant Muhammad, benefiting him especially and all creation generally.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r1.anchor: يعني على محمد القرآن , فتمدح بإنزاله لأنه أنعم عليه خصوصا , وعلىالخلق عموما .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.speaker: مقاتل
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.claim: ʿIwaj can mean inconsistency or contradiction.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r2.anchor: أحدها : يعني مختلفا , قاله مقاتل , ومنه قول الشاعر :

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r3.anchor: الثاني : يعني مخلوقا , قاله ابن عباس .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.speaker: علي بن عيسى
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.claim: ʿIwaj can mean departure from truth and straightness toward falsehood and corruption.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r4.anchor: الثالث : أنه العدول عن الحق إلى الباطل , وعن الاستقامة إلى الفساد , وهو قول علي بن عيسى .

MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.claim: With kasra, ʿiwaj describes religion, a path, or something not upright; with fatḥa, it describes upright objects such as reeds or wood.
MAWARDI-FULL:v3p283#2/r5.anchor: أن العوج بكسر العين ما كان في الدين وفي الطريق وفيما ليس بقائم منتصب , والعوج بفتح العين ما كان في القناة والخشبة

MUQATIL:18:1-2/r1.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r1.speaker: اليهود
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r1.claim: The Jews objected that Muhammad's book came differently, unlike the Torah, whose sections they said were revealed in separate places.
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r1.anchor: وذلك أن اليهود قالوا: يزعم محمد أنه لا ينزل عليه الكتاب مختلفا، فإن كان صادقا بأنه من الله

MUQATIL:18:1-2/r2.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r2.speaker: author
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r2.claim: The Qur'an has no inconsistency; awaj means different.
MUQATIL:18:1-2/r2.anchor: { ولم يجعل له عوجا } [آية: 1]، يعني مختلفا.

NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r1.claim: God teaches His servants to praise Him for Islam and the revealed Book, His greatest gifts and the means of their salvation.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r1.anchor: لقن الله عباده وفقهم كيف يثنون عليه ويحمدونه على أجزل نعمائه عليهم وهي نعمة الإسلام وما أنزل على محمد

NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r2.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r2.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r2.claim: The Book has no crookedness: its meanings contain no contradiction or departure from wisdom; crookedness in meanings is like crookedness in physical things.
NASAFI-FULL:v3p3/r2.anchor: والعوج في المعاني كالعوج في الأعيان يقال في رأيه عوج وفي عصاه عوج والمراد نفي الاختلاف و التناقض عن معانيه

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p263#2/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p263#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p263#2/r1.claim: The word order is advanced and delayed: the intended sense is that God sent down an upright book and made no crookedness in it.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p263#2/r1.anchor: مقدم ومؤخر. أراد: أنزل الكتاب قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r2.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3/r2.claim: The Book has no crookedness and is upright, with no inconsistency.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r2.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r2.speaker: الأخفش والكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد وجمهور المتأولين
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r2.claim: They analyze the opening as reordered: God sent the upright Book and did not make it crooked, with qayyiman in the accusative as a circumstantial phrase.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r2.anchor: وزعم الأخفش والكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد وجمهور المتأولين أن في أول هذه السورة تقديمًا وتأخيرًا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r3.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r3.speaker: قتادة
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r3.claim: Qatada reads the words in their stated order, supplying the sense 'He did not make it crooked, but made it upright.'
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r3.anchor: وقال قتادة: الكلام على سياقه من غير تقديم ولا تأخير،

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r4.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r4.speaker: الضحاك
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r4.claim: Al-Qurtubi commends al-Dahhak's explanation: the Book is upright in wisdom, with no error, corruption, or contradiction.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r4.anchor: وقول الضحاك فيه حسن، وأن المعنى: مستقيم، أي مستقيم الحكمة لا خطأ فيه

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r5.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r5.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r5.claim: Other readings make qayyiman confirm the earlier scriptures or serve as an enduring proof.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r5.anchor: وقيل: «قيما» على الكتب السابقة يصدقها. وقيل: «قيما» بالحجج أبدا.

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r6.claim: The form with kasra in awaj is used for religion, thought, affairs, and paths; with fatḥa it describes physical bodies such as wood and walls.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r6.anchor: والعوج بكسر العين في الدين والرأي والأمر والطريق. وبفتحها في الأجسام

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r7.claim: Awaj can mean flaw or contradiction; the Quran has no inconsistency, as 4:82 argues about a text from other than God.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r7.anchor:
أي ليس متناقضا مختلفا، كما قال تعالى:
ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r8.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r8.speaker: ابن عباس
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r8.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas glosses 'not having awaj' as meaning the Quran is uncreated, as in 39:28.
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r8.anchor:
كما روي عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى:
قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج

QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r9.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r9.speaker: مقاتل
QURTUBI-FULL:18:1-3#4/r9.claim: Muqatil explains awaj as disagreement or variation.

RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.claim: Tasbih precedes praise in scriptural wording: God is glorified when the Night Journey is mentioned but praised when revelation of the Book is mentioned.
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r1.anchor: أن التسبيح أينما جاء فإنما جاء مقدما على التحميد ، ألا ترى أنه يقال : { سبحان الله * والحمد لله }

RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.claim: Glorification comes first because it declares God perfect in Himself; praise follows because He perfects others, so the Night Journey is an initial rank and scripture's teaching humanity is the higher culmination.
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r2.anchor: أن التسبيح أول الأمر لأنه عبارة عن تنزيه الله عما لا ينبغي وهو إشارة إلى كونه كاملا في ذاته

RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.claim: A report says whoever learns and teaches is called great in the heavens, illustrating the servant's highest station as learned and teaching others.
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r3.anchor: ولهذا روي في الخبر أنه عليه الصلاة والسلام قال : ( من تعلم وعلم فذاك يدعى عظيما في السموات )

RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.claim: The Night Journey raises the Prophet's person from below to above, while revelation brings the light of inspiration from above to him; the latter is greater.
RAZI-FULL:v21p62#2/r4.anchor: الإسراء عبارة عن رفع ذاته من تحت إلى فوق وإنزال الكتاب عليه عبارة عن إنزال نور الوحي عليه من فوق إلى تحت

RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r2.speaker: المشبهة
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r2.claim: The anthropomorphists use the language of the Night Journey and revelation's descent to argue that God occupies the upper direction; Razi refers the answer to the discussion of God's throne.
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r2.anchor: المشبهة استدلوا بلفظ الإسراء في السورة المتقدمة وبلفظ الإنزال في هذه السورة على أنه تعالى مختص بجهة فوق

RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r3.claim: Revelation benefited Muhammad by disclosing profound knowledge of monotheism, divine attributes, angels and prophets, decree, the two worlds, and the soul's vision of the unseen realm.
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r3.anchor: أطلعه بواسطة هذا الكتاب الكريم على أسرار علوم التوحيد والتنزيه وصفات الجلال والإكرام وأسرار أحوال الملائكة والأنبياء

RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r4.claim: The Quran benefits the community through duties, laws, promises, warnings, reward, and punishment; each person gains according to capacity, so Messenger and believers must praise God for it.
RAZI-FULL:v21p63/r4.anchor: فلأنه مشتمل على التكاليف والأحكام والوعد والوعيد والثواب والعقاب

RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r1.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r1.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r1.claim: The Book's lack of crookedness can mean its verses contain no contradictions, as established by the cited verse.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r1.anchor: نفي التناقض عن آياته كما قال : { ولو كان من عند غير الله لوجدوا فيه اختلافا كثيرا } ( النساء : 82 )

RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r2.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r2.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r2.claim: Another sense is that everything the Book says about monotheism, prophethood, laws, and obligations is entirely true and free of flaw.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r2.anchor: أن كل ما ذكر الله من التوحيد والنبوة والأحكام والتكاليف فهو حق وصدق ولا خلل في شيء منها البتة

RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r3.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r3.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r3.claim: A further reading sees the Book as free of deviation because it directs humanity from worldly bodily concerns toward the afterlife, spiritual realities, and God.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r3.anchor: فكل ما دعاه في الدنيا إلى الآخرة ومن الجسمانيات إلى الروحانيات ومن الخلق إلى الحق

RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r6.speaker: الواحدي
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r6.claim: Al-Wahidi and other linguists treat the order as inversion, reading a straight Book with no crookedness; Razi rejects this because intrinsic perfection precedes the Book's role in perfecting others.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64/r6.anchor: قال الواحدي جميع أهل اللغة والتفسير قالوا هذا من التقديم والتأخير والتقدير : أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما

RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r12.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r12.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r12.claim: Al-Qadi argues the Quran is created: it is described as sent down and descended, as a compiled Book of letters and words, as a bestowed benefit deserving praise, and as straight rather than crooked, a quality he says cannot describe the eternal.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r12.anchor: قال القاضي : الآية دالة على صحة قولنا في مسائل ، أحدها : أن القرآن مخلوق وبيانه من وجوه

RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r13.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r13.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r13.claim: Al-Qadi argues for human freedom from the command to praise: scriptural guidance can benefit people only if they independently choose whether to act or abstain.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r13.anchor: نفس الأمر بالحمد لأنه لو لم يكن للعبد فعل لم ينتفع بالكتاب إذ الانتفاع به إنما يحصل إذا قدر على أن يفعل

RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r14.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r14.speaker: القاضي
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r14.claim: He argues that if God revealed passages to cause some people to disbelieve and others to believe, it would be hard to call the Book upright.
RAZI-FULL:v21p64#2/r14.anchor: والثاني : أنه تعالى لو كان أنزل بعض الكتاب ليكون سببا لكفر البعض وأنزل الباقي ليؤمن البعض الآخر

STUDYQURAN:18:1/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r1.speaker: IK
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r1.claim: Some describe the Quran as God’s greatest gift to humanity because it brings people from darkness into light; the servant is the Prophet.
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r1.anchor: described by some as God’s greatest gift to humanity, since it brings them from darkness into light (IK). His servant refers to the Prophet.

STUDYQURAN:18:1/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r2.speaker: Ṭs, Z
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r2.claim: The Quran’s lack of crookedness means it has no contradictions or discrepancies.
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r2.anchor: widely understood to mean that it contains no contradictions or discrepancies (Ṭs, Z)

STUDYQURAN:18:1/r3.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r3.speaker: R, Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r3.claim: Others understand the phrase as denying corruption or falsehood in the Quran.
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r3.anchor: understood to mean that the Quran contains no corruption or falsehood (R, Ṭs)

STUDYQURAN:18:1/r4.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r4.speaker: Ṭs
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r4.claim: The Quran also remains continuously beneficial and guides people toward the straight path.
STUDYQURAN:18:1/r4.anchor: that it remains continuously beneficial (Ṭs) as it guides people toward the straight path (IK)

STUDYQURAN:18:2/r5.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:18:2/r5.speaker: al-Qāḍī ʿAbd al-Jabbār
STUDYQURAN:18:2/r5.claim: He argues these verses support the Muʿtazilite view that the Quran is created: descent and being made upright imply change and making, unlike the eternal uncreated Quran of the Ashʿarites.
STUDYQURAN:18:2/r5.anchor: the Muʿtazilite theologian al-QāḍīʿAbd al-Jabbār argued

NAHHAS:v2p447/r1.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v2p447/r1.speaker: الأخفش سعيد، الكسائي، الفراء، أبو عبيد
NAHHAS:v2p447/r1.claim: These grammarians propose fronting and postponement at the surah’s opening: the sense is praise to God, who sent the Book to His servant as upright, without crookedness.
NAHHAS:v2p447/r1.anchor: زعم الأخفش سعيد والكسائي والفراء وأبو عبيد أن في أول هذه السورة تقديما وتأخيرا

TABATABAI:18:2/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:2/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:2/r1.claim: The sūrah calls people to true belief and good action through warning and glad tidings, as its opening and closing make clear; it gives special emphasis to rejecting the claim that God has a child.
TABATABAI:18:2/r1.anchor: تتضمن الدعوة إلى الاعتقاد الحق والعمل الصالح بالإنذار والتبشير

TABATABAI:18:2/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.claim: The sūrah may have been revealed to present three unusual narratives found nowhere else in the Qurʾān—the Companions of the Cave, Moses and his companion, and Dhū al-Qarnayn—and derive lessons against associating partners and for piety.
TABATABAI:18:2/r3.anchor: ذكر القصص الثلاث العجيبة التي لم تذكر في القرآن الكريم إلا في هذه السورة

TABATABAI:18:1-8/r1.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r1.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r1.claim: The interpretation that the verse tells people to say praise to God is not sound; the verse itself praises God for revealing the scripture.
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r1.anchor: يعني قولوا الحمد لله الذي نزل

TABATABAI:18:1-8/r2.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r2.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r2.claim: The pronoun in the no-crookedness clause refers to the Book; both that clause and qayyiman are circumstantial descriptions of it, an arrangement the context supports over alternate parses.
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r2.anchor: وقوله { ولم يجعل له عوجا } الضمير للكتاب والجملة حال عن الكتاب وقوله { قيما } حال بعد حال على ما يفيده السياق

TABATABAI:18:1-8/r3.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r3.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r3.claim: Other parses make the no-crookedness clause coordinate with the relative clause, attach qayyiman to its pronoun, supply an omitted verb, or reverse the order; he rejects them as contrary to the context.
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r3.anchor: وقيل إن جملة { ولم يجعل له عوجا } معطوفة على الصلة و { قيما } حال من ضمير { له }

TABATABAI:18:1-8/r4.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r4.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r4.claim: Negated indefinite ʿawajan is universal: the Qurʾān has no deviation in language, meaning, guidance, proof, counsel, narrative, judgment, protection, or consistency, and falsehood cannot reach it.
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r4.anchor: ووقوع { عوجا } وهو نكرة في سياق النفي يفيد العموم فالقرآن مستقيم في جميع جهاته

TABATABAI:18:1-8/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r5.claim: Qayyim means managing a thing's interests; the Qurʾān's true belief and good action constitute the upright religion that serves humanity in this life and the next.
TABATABAI:18:1-8/r5.anchor: والكتاب إنما يكون قيما بما يشتمل عليه من المعاني، والذي يتضمنه القرآن هو الاعتقاد الحق والعمل الصالح

TABATABAI:18:2-5/r5.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:18:2-5/r5.speaker: author
TABATABAI:18:2-5/r5.claim: Other interpretations take qayyim as balanced without excess or deficiency, or as governing, affirming, preserving, and abrogating earlier scriptures; the context supports the author's account of the Qurʾān as serving human interests.
TABATABAI:18:2-5/r5.anchor: وقيل المراد بالقيم المستقيم المعتدل الذي لا إفراط فيه ولا تفريط، وقيل القيم المدبر لسائر الكتب السماوية

THALABI:v6p144#4/r1.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p144#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس
THALABI:v6p144#4/r1.claim: He glosses the upright book as just.

THALABI:v6p144#4/r2.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p144#4/r2.speaker: الفراء
THALABI:v6p144#4/r2.claim: The Quran is upright over all scriptures and abrogates their laws.
THALABI:v6p144#4/r2.anchor: الفراء: قيما على الكتب كلها ناسخا لشرائعها.

THALABI:v6p144#4/r3.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v6p144#4/r3.speaker: author
THALABI:v6p144#4/r3.claim: The book is straight and free of contradiction; it warns of severe punishment and gives believers glad tidings of Paradise and an everlasting reward.
THALABI:v6p144#4/r3.anchor: الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما مستقيما. قال ابن عباس

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r1.speaker: ابن عباس عن الوالبي
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r1.claim: He glosses ʿiwajan as confusion or ambiguity, so the book is not unclear or crooked.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r1.anchor: روى الوالبي عن ابن عباس في قوله: {ولم يجعل له عوجا} قال:

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r2.speaker: أبو إسحاق
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r2.claim: He says the book contains no contradiction, as in 4:82.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r2.anchor: وقال أبو إسحاق: (لم يجعل فيه اختلافا)

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r3.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r3.speaker: ابن عباس
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r3.claim: He glosses qayyiman as upright and just, a meaning also discussed at 6:161.

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r4.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r4.speaker: أهل اللغة والتفسير
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r4.claim: They take the wording as fronted and delayed: the book was sent down upright, without crookedness.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p519#4/r4.anchor: وجميع أهل اللغة والتفسير قالوا: (هذا من التقديم والتأخير،

WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p533/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p533/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p533/r1.claim: The surah opens by praising God and affirming the Prophet's mission in answer to those who denied it; the Qur'an warns and gives good news, then warns Quraysh for claiming the angels are God's daughters.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v13p533/r1.anchor: وافتتح السورة تبارك وتعالى بحمده وذكر نبوة رسوله لما أنكروه عليه

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:1-2/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:1-2/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:1-2/r1.claim: The Book has no inconsistency or ambiguity.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:18:1-2/r1.anchor: { الحمد لله الذي أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا } اختلافا والتباسا.

YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p171/r1.author: Yaḥyā b. Sallām
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p171/r1.speaker: author
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p171/r1.claim: God praises Himself because He is worthy of praise; His servant is Muhammad, and the Book is the Qur'an.
YAHYA-SALLAM:v1p171/r1.anchor: قوله: {الحمد لله} [سورة الكهف: 1] حمد نفسه، وهو أهل الحمد. {الذي أنزل على عبده} [الكهف: 1] محمد. {الكتاب} [الكهف: 1] القرآن.

ELMALILI:17:110-111/r16.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r16.speaker: author
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r16.claim: The next surah's opening praise harmonizes with Isra ending in praise and magnification.
ELMALILI:17:110-111/r16.anchor: Sûre-i Kehf’in hamd ile başlaması ne ahenkdârdır.

ELMALILI:18:1-3/r1.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:18:1-3/r1.speaker: author
ELMALILI:18:1-3/r1.claim: God sent the Book without crookedness: it is straight, authoritative, and free of falsehood or error.
ELMALILI:18:1-3/r1.anchor: dolambaçlı değil, çarpık değil, yalanı yanlışı yok

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:1/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:1/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:1/r1.claim: Because the Qur’an is the greatest blessing, praise and reverence belong to the God who sent it; “servant” means Muhammad and “book” means the Qur’an.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:18:1/r1.anchor: Buradaki “kul”dan maksat Hz. Muhammed, “kitap”tan maksat da Kur’an-ı Kerîm’dir.

SAMIN-DURR:18:1/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:18:1/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:18:1/r1.claim: Wa-lam yajʿal may coordinate with the preceding relative clause, interrupt parenthetically between qayyiman and its antecedent, or function as a circumstance of the Book; this determines qayyiman’s analysis.
SAMIN-DURR:18:1/r1.anchor: في هذه الجملة أوجه، أحدها: أنها معطوفة على الصلة قبلها. والثاني: أنها اعتراضية بين الحال وهي

ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r2.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r2.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r2.claim: ʿIwaj with kasra describes something without a visible body, such as religion; ʿawaj with fatḥa describes a physical thing such as a stick.
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r2.anchor: والعوج - بكسر العين - فيما لا يرى له شخص، وما كان له شخص قيل فيه عوج بفتح العين.

ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r3.claim: The verse thanks God for sending Muhammad a straight book without disagreement, as the Qur’an says a book from other than God would contain many differences.
ZAJJAJ:v3p267/r3.anchor: وتأويله الشكر لله الذي أنزل على محمد الكتاب مستقيما

ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r1.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r1.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r1.claim: Iwaj can mean crookedness, tortuousness, deviation, distortion, or deviousness.

ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r2.author: Muhammad Asad
ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r2.speaker: author
ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r2.claim: The phrase presents the Qur'an as direct and unambiguous, free of obscurities and internal contradictions, with 4:82 as a parallel.
ASAD-NOTES:18:1#n1/r2.anchor: meant to establish the direct, unambiguous character of the Qur'an and to stress its freedom from all obscurities and internal contradictions

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Like the previous sūrah, al-Kahf was revealed in the late Makkan conflict, as Quraysh sought to erase the Qur’ānic mission while Jews and Christians backed them indirectly.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Like the previous sūrah, this sūrah was also revealed in that part of the Makkan period when the conflict between good and evil of the Prophet’s preaching mission had entered its final phase.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Quraysh are warned not to let worldly success lead them to reject an obvious truth, since God’s punishment is near if they persist in arrogance.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Quryash are warned that in the wake of their worldly successes they should not try to arrogantly deny an obvious reality.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet and companions are urged to patience and steadfastness, with hints of migration and glad tidings of coming victories granted by God.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) and his companions are urged to be patient and steadfast. Certain subtle indications are made of the upcoming phases of migration

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: Where the previous sūrah exposed Jews, al-Kahf and Maryam expose Christians; Quraysh risk losing the great opportunity God offers if they follow baseless opponents in rejecting it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: Just as in the previous sūrah, S ūrah Banī Isrā’īl, the Jews are exposed, in this sūrah and in the next one – S ūrah Maryam – the Christians are exposed.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: The Prophet’s task is to warn and give glad tidings; unbelief among rebels reflects neither a defect in the Book nor a shortcoming in his preaching.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The Prophet (sws) is urged to be patient since his only responsibility is to warn and give glad tidings to his nation.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.claim: People’s blindness comes from infatuation with worldly lures; the Prophet should not fret, because the world’s false ornament will be exposed and they will regret their conduct.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-4-surah-yunus-10-sur.anchor: The reason for this is that these people have become blind in their infatuation with the lures of this world.

QIRAAT-ER:18:1:13#1/r1.author: QIRAAT-ER
QIRAAT-ER:18:1:13#1/r1.speaker: author
QIRAAT-ER:18:1:13#1/r1.claim: Pausing after ʿiwajā separates it from qayyimā in 18:2 and affects whether the two verses form one sentence or two.
QIRAAT-ER:18:1:13#1/r1.anchor: Waqf variant: pause on ʿiwajā separating it from qayyimā in 18:2 — affects whether 18:1-2 are one sentence

ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p396#2/r1.author: ʿAbd al-Razzāq al-Ṣanʿānī
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p396#2/r1.speaker: قتادة
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p396#2/r1.claim: Qatāda says God sent down the Book upright and free of crookedness.
ABDURRAZZAQ:v2p396#2/r1.anchor: عن قتادة في قوله تعالى ﴿ ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما ﴾ قال أنزل الله الكتاب قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا

TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.claim: Al-Ṭabarī says revelation has four names in Arabic—Qur'an, Furqān, Kitāb, and Dhikr—and each has a distinct meaning and usage.
TAB-FULL:v1p89#2/r1.anchor: سمى تنزيله الذي أنزله على نبيه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم، أسماء أربعة: منهن القرآن

TAB-FULL:v1p94/r3.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r3.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r3.claim: An unnamed poet's divorce verse calls the written divorce document a kitāb, illustrating that a written object may take the name of the act that produced it.
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r3.anchor: في صفة كتاب طلاق، كتبه لامرأته

TAB-FULL:v1p94/r9.author: al-Ṭabarī
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r9.speaker: author
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r9.claim: Kitāb is a verbal noun from writing, like qiyām from standing and ḥisāb from reckoning; it denotes the writer's joined or separate letters, though the Qur'an itself is written.
TAB-FULL:v1p94/r9.anchor: وأما تأويل اسمه الذي هو الكتاب فهو مصدر من قولك كتبت كتابا، كما تقول قمت قياما، وحسبت الشيء حسابا

BURHAN:v1p38/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p38/r10.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p38/r10.claim: Al-Isrāʾ opens with glorification and al-Kahf with praise, reflecting the usual order of the paired phrases “Glory be to God, and praise be to God.”
BURHAN:v1p38/r10.anchor: وكذلك مناسبة فاتحة سورة الإسراء بالتسبيح وسورة الكهف بالتحميد لأن التسبيح حيث جاء مقدم على التحميد

BURHAN:v1p364/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p364/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p364/r1.claim: An incomplete pause after ʿiwajā clarifies that qayyiman is separate from ʿiwajā and is a circumstantial phrase whose syntactic position is advanced.
BURHAN:v1p364/r1.anchor: منها أن يكون لضرب من البيان كقوله تعالى ﴿ ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما ﴾ إذ به تبين أن قيما منفصل عن عوجا

BURHAN:v3p277/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r2.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v3p277/r2.claim: Al-Wāḥidī and others propose fronting and postponement: the sense is that God revealed the book upright and made no crookedness in it.
BURHAN:v3p277/r2.anchor: الآية أي أنزله قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا قاله جماعة منهم الواحدي

BURHAN:v3p277/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r3.speaker: فخر الدين الرازي
BURHAN:v3p277/r3.claim: Al-Rāzī rejects that reordered reading: the book is complete in itself before it completes others, so the verse’s stated order is rationally correct and the proposed reversal impossible.

BURHAN:v3p277/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r4.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p277/r4.claim: The author calls al-Rāzī’s objection a surprising misunderstanding: proponents discuss word order for syntax, not the order in which the meanings become true; and if qayyim means upholding others, no reversal is needed.
BURHAN:v3p277/r4.anchor: وهذا فهم عجيب من الإمام لأن القائل بالتقديم والتأخير لا يقول بأن كونه غير ذي عوج متأخر

BURHAN:v3p277/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p277/r5.claim: The more apparent parse places the clause making no crookedness within the relative clause of الذي, where it has no independent syntactic position.
BURHAN:v3p277/r5.anchor: أحدهما أن الأظهر جعل هذه الجملة أعنى قوله

BURHAN:v3p277/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p277/r6.speaker: جماعة
BURHAN:v3p277/r6.claim: A further parse makes the clause a circumstantial accusative from the book, governed by أنزل; on this analysis, the order is fronted and postponed and the clause is parenthetic.
BURHAN:v3p277/r6.anchor: ويجوز في الجملة المذكورة أن يكون موضعها النصب على أنها حال من الكتاب والعامل فيها أنزل قاله جماعة

BURHAN:v1p273/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r1.claim: Zarkashī catalogs Qur’anic names including admonition, reminder, noble, exalted, wisdom, wise, guardian, blessed, and the rope of God.

BURHAN:v1p273/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.claim: His catalog continues with the straight path, qayyim, decisive word, great news, best discourse, revelation, spirit, inspiration, and the seven oft-repeated verses.
BURHAN:v1p273/r2.anchor: وسماه الصراط المستقيم فقال ﴿ وأن هذا

BURHAN:v1p273/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.speaker: author
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.claim: The remaining names include Arabic, connected speech, insight, clarification, knowledge, truth, guidance, wonder, reminder, the firmest bond, similitudes, and truthfulness; Ibn ʿAbbās says the Qur’an is uncreated.
BURHAN:v1p273/r3.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال

BURHAN:v1p273/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p273/r4.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v1p273/r4.claim: Commenting on the Qur’an being named Arabic, Ibn ʿAbbās says it is uncreated.
BURHAN:v1p273/r4.anchor: قال ابن عباس غير مخلوق وسماه قولا فقال

BURHAN:v1p343/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p343/r1.speaker: أبو بكر بن مجاهد
BURHAN:v1p343/r1.claim: Ibn Mujahid says sound pausal decisions require mastery of grammar, readings, exegesis and narratives, discerning their summaries, and the Arabic of revelation.
BURHAN:v1p343/r1.anchor: قال أبو بكر بن مجاهد لا يقوم بالتمام في الوقف إلا نحوى عالم بالقراءات عالم بالتفسير والقصص

BURHAN:v1p343/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v1p343/r4.speaker: قتادة
BURHAN:v1p343/r4.claim: Pause after عوجا and begin قيما, lest قيما be mistaken for an adjective of عوج, since crookedness cannot be upright; Ibn al-Nahhas attributes this stop to Qatada.
BURHAN:v1p343/r4.anchor: لئلا يتخيل كونه صفة له إذا العوج لا يكون قيما وقد حكاه ابن النحاس عن قتادة

BURHAN:v3p278/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p278/r1.claim: One proposed parsing makes قيما the object of an implicit verb, estimated as ولكن جعله قيما.
BURHAN:v3p278/r1.anchor: والثاني أن يكون منصوبا بفعل مقدر وتقديره ولكن جعله قيما فيكون مفعولا للفعل المقدر

BURHAN:v3p278/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r2.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p278/r2.claim: Another parsing treats قيما as an emphatic circumstantial accusative referring to the pronoun in ولم يجعل له عوجا.
BURHAN:v3p278/r2.anchor: أن يكون حالا من الضمير في قوله

BURHAN:v3p278/r3.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r3.speaker: الزمخشري
BURHAN:v3p278/r3.claim: Al-Zamakhshari prefers an implicit verb governing قيما, because making it circumstantial would interrupt the relative clause before it is complete.
BURHAN:v3p278/r3.anchor: لأن الجملة التي قبلها عنده معطوفة على الصلة

BURHAN:v3p278/r4.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r4.speaker: ابن المنير
BURHAN:v3p278/r4.claim: Ibn al-Munayyir argues that both clauses can be consecutive circumstantial clauses describing the same book: it was sent down without crookedness.
BURHAN:v3p278/r4.anchor: بل هما حالان متواليان من شيء واحد والتقدير أنزل الكتاب غير معوج

BURHAN:v3p278/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r5.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p278/r5.claim: The author favors an independent coordinated clause because it denies crookedness of the book absolutely, not only at the time of revelation, which is the fuller point.
BURHAN:v3p278/r5.anchor: لأن جعل الجملة حالا يفيده لا ما يفيد العطف من نفي العوج عن الكتاب مطلقا غير مقيد بالإنزال وهو المقصود

BURHAN:v3p278/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r6.speaker: جماعة
BURHAN:v3p278/r6.claim: The circumstantial-clause analysis was proposed by scholars before Ibn al-Munayyir.
BURHAN:v3p278/r6.anchor: وهذا القول وهو جعل الجملة حالا قد ذكره جماعة قبل ابن المنير

BURHAN:v3p278/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r7.speaker: ابن عباس
BURHAN:v3p278/r7.claim: The word-order reversal analysis is transmitted from Ibn Abbas, as cited by al-Tabari and others.
BURHAN:v3p278/r7.anchor: والقول بالتقديم والتأخير منقول عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما نقله الطبري وغيره

BURHAN:v3p278/r8.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r8.speaker: الواحدي
BURHAN:v3p278/r8.claim: Al-Wahidi calls the transmitted word-order analysis the view of all linguists and exegetes; al-Zamakhshari may have noted it, allowed other analyses, but judged his own best.
BURHAN:v3p278/r8.anchor: وقال الواحدي هو قول جميع أهل اللغة والتفسير والزمخشري ربما لاحظ هذا المعنى ولم يمنع جواز غير ما قال لكن ما قال هو الأحسن

BURHAN:v3p278/r9.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r9.speaker: غير ابن المنير
BURHAN:v3p278/r9.claim: Another objection to al-Zamakhshari says coordination keeps the independent clause inside the relative clause, so there is no interruption.
BURHAN:v3p278/r9.anchor: وقال غير ابن المنير في الاعتراض على الزمخشري إن الجملة وإن كانت مستقلة فهي في حيز الصلة للعطف فلم يقع فصل

BURHAN:v3p278/r10.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r10.speaker: حفص عن عاصم
BURHAN:v3p278/r10.claim: Hafs's slight pause after عوجا supports an inferred break between that clause and قيما.
BURHAN:v3p278/r10.anchor: ويؤيد ما ذكره صاحب الكشاف أن بعض القراء يسكت عند قوله عوجا ويفصل بينه وبين قيما بسكتة لطيفة وهي رواية حفص عن عاصم

BURHAN:v3p278/r11.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p278/r11.speaker: ابن المنير
BURHAN:v3p278/r11.claim: Ibn al-Munayyir also explains Hafs's pause as preventing قيما from being mistaken for an adjective of عوجا: indefinite nouns often take adjectives, including صراطا مستقيما and قرآنا عربيا.
BURHAN:v3p278/r11.anchor: قال ابن المنير وتحتمل السكتة وجها آخر وهو أن يكون ذلك لرفع توهم أن يكون قيما نعتا للعوج لأن النكرة تستدعي النعت غالبا

BURHAN:v3p279/r1.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r1.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p279/r1.claim: The author prefers his earlier analysis of qayyiman: it cannot describe ʿiwajan because opposites do not qualify one another.
BURHAN:v3p279/r1.anchor: فإن الشيء لا يوصف بضده لأن العوج لا يكون قيما

BURHAN:v3p279/r2.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p279/r2.speaker: بعضهم
BURHAN:v3p279/r2.claim: Some make qayyiman a substitute for ʿiwajan; the author finds this syntactically unclear.
BURHAN:v3p279/r2.anchor: نقل الإمام عن بعضهم أن قيما بدل من قوله عوجا وهو مشكل

ITQAN:v1p229#3/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r4.claim: An incomplete stop after ʿiwajan clarifies that qayyiman is separate and functions as a circumstantial accusative intended to precede it.
ITQAN:v1p229#3/r4.anchor: كقوله ﴿ ولم يجعل له عوجا ﴾ فإن الوقف هنا يبين أن ﴿ قيما ﴾ منفصل عنه وأنه حال في نية التقديم

ITQAN:v1p49/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.claim: The listed exceptions in al-Kahf are its opening through 'barren ground', the command to keep patient company, and 'those who believe' through the sūra's end.
ITQAN:v1p49/r6.anchor: الكهف استثني من أولها إلى ﴿ جرزا ﴾ وقوله ﴿ واصبر نفسك ﴾ الآية

ITQAN:v3p11/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p11/r1.claim: The deviant in heart rushes to difficult questions and tries to understand ambiguous passages before mastering the foundational teachings, reversing the proper order of study.
ITQAN:v3p11/r1.anchor: ومراد هذا الذي في قلبه زيغ التقدم إلى المشكلات وفهم المتشابه قبل فهم الأمهات

ITQAN:v3p11/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r2.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p11/r2.claim: Such people resemble pagans who suppose they would believe if given different signs, not knowing that faith comes only by God’s permission.
ITQAN:v3p11/r2.anchor: ومثل هؤلاء مثل المشركين الذين يقترحون على رسلهم آيات غير الآيات التي جاءوا بها ويظنون أنهم لو جاءتهم آيات أخر

ITQAN:v3p11/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r3.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r3.claim: Al-Raghib classifies passages as unequivocally clear, unequivocally ambiguous, or clear in one respect and ambiguous in another.
ITQAN:v3p11/r3.anchor: وقال الراغب في مفردات القرآن الآيات عند اعتبار بعضها ببعض ثلاثة أضرب محكم على الإطلاق ومتشابه على الإطلاق

ITQAN:v3p11/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r4.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r4.claim: Ambiguity in individual words can arise from rare vocabulary, such as al-abb and yaziffūn, or from a word with multiple senses, such as hand or right hand.
ITQAN:v3p11/r4.anchor: فالأول ضربان أحدهما يرجع إلى الألفاظ المفردة إما من جهة الغرابة نحو ( الأب ) و ( يزفون )

ITQAN:v3p11/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r5.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r5.claim: Ambiguity in a whole utterance can arise from concision, expansion, or word order; al-Raghib illustrates the first two with the orphan-marriage wording and the denial of any likeness to God.
ITQAN:v3p11/r5.anchor: وثانيهما يرجع إلى جملة الكلام المركب وذلك ثلاثة أضرب ضرب لاختصار الكلام نحو ﴿ وإن خفتم ألا تقسطوا في اليتامى فانكحوا ما طاب لكم ﴾

ITQAN:v3p11/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r6.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r6.claim: Al-Raghib treats the wording as an instance of ambiguous order and parses it as: He sent down the Book upright and did not make it crooked.
ITQAN:v3p11/r6.anchor: وضرب لنظم الكلام نحو ﴿ أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما ﴾ تقديره ( أنزل على عبده الكتاب قيما

ITQAN:v3p11/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r7.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r7.claim: Ambiguity limited to meaning includes descriptions of God and the Resurrection, which human imagination cannot picture because they are not sensed or of a familiar kind.
ITQAN:v3p11/r7.anchor: والمتشابه من جهة المعنى أوصاف الله تعالى وأوصاف القيامة فإن تلك الأوصاف لا تتصور لنا

ITQAN:v3p11/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p11/r8.speaker: الراغب
ITQAN:v3p11/r8.claim: Passages ambiguous in both wording and meaning can vary by quantity, legal force, time, or place and circumstances of revelation.

ITQAN:v3p33/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p33/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v3p33/r1.claim: One class of passages appears difficult until its order is recognized as precedence and postponement; early authorities identified such cases in verses.
ITQAN:v3p33/r1.anchor: الأول ما أشكل معناه بحسب الظاهر فلما عرف أنه من باب التقديم والتأخير اتضح

ITQAN:v3p33/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p33/r4.speaker: مجاهد
ITQAN:v3p33/r4.claim: Mujahid says the order is advanced and postponed: God sent down the Book upright, and did not make it crooked.
ITQAN:v3p33/r4.anchor: وأخرج عن مجاهد في قوله تعالى ﴿ أنزل على عبده الكتاب ولم يجعل له عوجا قيما ﴾ قال هذا من التقديم والتأخير

ITQAN:v1p35/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p35/r1.claim: One definition classifies as Makkan what was revealed in Mecca, even after the Hijra, and as Medinan what was revealed in Medina; revelations during travel fit neither label.
ITQAN:v1p35/r1.anchor: الثاني أن المكي ما نزل بمكة ولو بعد الهجرة والمدني ما نزل بالمدينة وعلى هذا تثبت الواسطة فما نزل بالأسفار لا يطلق عليه مكي ولا مدني

ITQAN:v1p35/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r2.speaker: أبو أمامة
ITQAN:v1p35/r2.claim: A report attributed to the Prophet says the Qur’an was revealed in three places: Mecca, Medina, and Syria; al-Walid identifies Syria as Jerusalem.
ITQAN:v1p35/r2.anchor: وقد أخرج الطبراني في الكبير من طريق الوليد بن مسلم عن عفير بن معدان عن ابن عامر عن أبي أمامة قال قال رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم أنزل القرآن في ثلاثة أمكنة مكة والمدينة والشام

ITQAN:v1p35/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r3.speaker: ابن كثير
ITQAN:v1p35/r3.claim: Ibn Kathir prefers taking the report’s reference to Syria as Tabuk rather than Jerusalem.
ITQAN:v1p35/r3.anchor: وقال الشيخ عماد الدين بن كثير بل تفسيره بتبوك أحسن

ITQAN:v1p35/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p35/r4.claim: The geographical labels include nearby sites: Mina, ʿArafat, and al-Hudaybiyya count with Mecca; Badr, Uhud, and Sila count with Medina.
ITQAN:v1p35/r4.anchor: قلت ويدخل في مكة ضواحيها كالمنزل بمنى وعرفات والحديبية وفي المدينة ضواحيها كالمنزل ببدر وأحد وسلع

ITQAN:v1p35/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r5.speaker: author
ITQAN:v1p35/r5.claim: Another definition calls a passage Makkan or Medinan according to whether its address is directed to the people of Mecca or Medina; this is how the author understands a later report from Ibn Masud.
ITQAN:v1p35/r5.anchor: الثالث أن المكي ما وقع خطابا لأهل مكة والمدني ما وقع خطابا لأهل المدينة وحمل على هذا قول ابن مسعود الآتي

ITQAN:v1p35/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r6.speaker: أبو بكر
ITQAN:v1p35/r6.claim: Qadi Abu Bakr says Makkan and Medinan status is known from the Companions and Successors, not a Prophetic statement; dating may be needed to identify abrogation but can be known without a Prophetic text.
ITQAN:v1p35/r6.anchor: قال القاضي أبو بكر في الانتصار إنما يرجع في معرفة المكي والمدني إلى حفظ الصحابة والتابعين ولم يرد عن النبي

ITQAN:v1p35/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r7.speaker: ابن مسعود
