ITQAN:v1p35/r7.claim: Ibn Masud swears that no Qur’anic verse came down without his knowing about whom and where it was revealed; al-Bukhari transmits the statement.
ITQAN:v1p35/r7.anchor: وقد أخرج البخاري عن ابن مسعود أنه قال والذي لا إله غيره ما نزلت آية من كتاب الله تعالى إلا وأنا أعلم فيمن نزلت

ITQAN:v1p35/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r8.speaker: عكرمة
ITQAN:v1p35/r8.claim: A man asked ʿIkrima about a verse, and ʿIkrima pointed to the slope of Mount Sila as its place of revelation; Abu Nuʿaym records it.
ITQAN:v1p35/r8.anchor: وقال أيوب سأل رجل عكرمة عن آية من القرآن فقال نزلت في سفح ذلك الجبل وأشار إلى سلع

ITQAN:v1p35/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v1p35/r9.speaker: ابن عباس
ITQAN:v1p35/r9.claim: Ibn Abbas says, in a report from Ubayy ibn Kaʿb, that twenty-seven surahs were revealed in Medina and the rest in Mecca.
ITQAN:v1p35/r9.anchor: قال ابن سعد في الطبقات أنبأنا الواقدي حدثني قدامة بن موسى عن أبي سلمة الحضرمي سمعت ابن عباس قال سألت أبي بن كعب

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r1.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r1.claim: An early authority says the Qur’an has thirty modes, including Makkan and Medinan, abrogating and abrogated, clear and ambiguous, precedence and postponement, connected and separate wording, causes, ellipsis, general and particular, commands, prohibitions, promises, threats, rulings, reports, questions, argument, admonition, parable, and oath.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r1.anchor: قال بعض الأقدمين أنزل القرآن على ثلاثين نحوا كل نحو منه غير صاحبه فمن عرف وجوهها

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r2.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r2.claim: The passage illustrates the Makkan category with a command to leave the disbelievers graciously.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r2.anchor: قال فالمكي مثل ﴿ واهجرهم هجرا جميلا ﴾

ITQAN:v3p94#2/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r3.speaker: بعض الأقدمين
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r3.claim: It illustrates the Medinan category with a command to fight in God’s way.
ITQAN:v3p94#2/r3.anchor: والمدني مثل ﴿ وقاتلوا في سبيل الله ﴾

ITQAN:v2p318/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p318/r1.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p318/r1.claim: ʿI waj means something crooked or convoluted.

ITQAN:v3p302/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p302/r1.speaker: الإمام
ITQAN:v3p302/r1.claim: An answer in al-Subki’s collection says glorification precedes praise wherever the two occur together, as in “glory be with praise” and “glory be to God and praise.”
ITQAN:v3p302/r1.anchor: سأل الأمام ما الحكمة في افتتاح سورة الإسراء بالتسبيح والكهف بالتحميد وأجاب بأن التسبيح حيث جاء مقدم على التحميد

ITQAN:v3p302/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v3p302/r3.speaker: ابن الزملكاني
ITQAN:v3p302/r3.claim: Ibn al-Zamalkani says al-Kahf opens with praise because it answered the polytheists’ question about the cave youths after revelation was delayed, assuring the Prophet that God had not withdrawn His favor and had completed it by sending the Book.
ITQAN:v3p302/r3.anchor: وسورة الكهف لما أنزلت بعد سؤال المشركين عن قصة أصحاب الكهف وتأخر الوحي نزلت مبينة أن الله لم يقطع نعمته

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r1.claim: Al-Farraʾ cites an Arab poem in which ناء describes the man leaning over the bow as he draws it.

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r2.claim: ما ساءك وناءك is explained as originally أناءك, with the initial alif dropped by sound-patterning after ساءك, as in هنأني ومرأني; alone, it would be أمرأني.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r2.anchor: وكان الأصل (أناءك) فألقي الألف لما اتبعه (ساءك)

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r6.claim: The order in 18:1–2 is advanced and delayed: God sent the Book down upright, and did not make it crooked.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p130/r6.anchor: أراد: أنزل الكتاب قيما ولم يجعل له عوجا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r1.claim: God guided people by the Book and made it upright, clear, and free of crookedness or falsehood; he calls it spirit, mercy, healing, guidance, and light.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r1.anchor: ولم يجعل له عوجا [الكهف: 1] بل نزله قيما مفصلا بينا

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r2.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r2.claim: The Qur’an’s inimitable composition defeats its opponents, while its recitation remains fresh, unwearied, and full of benefits and inexhaustible wonders; it supersedes earlier books.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r2.anchor: وقطع منه بمعجز التأليف أطماع الكائدين، وأبانه بعجيب النظم عن حيل المتكلفين

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r3.claim: The Qur’an gathers many meanings into few words, exemplifying the Prophet’s saying that he was given comprehensive speech.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p11/r3.anchor: وجمع الكثير من معانيه في القليل من لفظه، وذلك معنى

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r1.claim: The passage says that none of the caliphs completed the Qur’an except ʿUthmān.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r1.anchor: لم يختمه أحد من الخلفاء غير عثمان

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r2.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r2.speaker: الشعبي
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r2.claim: Al-Shaʿbī swore that ʿAlī entered his grave without having memorized the Qur’an.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r2.anchor: سمعت الشعبي يحلف بالله، عز وجل، لقد دخل علي حفرته وما حفظ القرآن

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r3.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r3.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r3.claim: Repeated prophetic stories let scattered tribes, each taught different sūras, hear the accounts of all the prophets and retain their warning.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r3.anchor: فلو لم تكن الأنباء والقصص مثناة ومكررة لوقعت قصة موسى إلى قوم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r4.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r4.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r4.claim: Stories differ from prescribed duties: the Prophet’s letters taught prayer, alms, fasting, and pilgrimage details that stories could not convey.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r4.anchor: وليست القصص كالفروض، لأن كتب رسول الله، صلى الله عليه وسلم كانت تنفذ إلى كل قوم

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r5.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r5.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r5.claim: This repetition served early Islam; after the religion spread, elders taught the young, and the Qur’an was collected, its rationale disappeared.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r5.anchor: فلما نشره الله عز وجل في كل قطر، وبثه في آفاق الأرض، وعلم الأكابر الأصاغر

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r6.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r6.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r6.claim: Arabic repeats speech for emphasis and understanding, and varies topics rather than restricting a speaker to one mode; examples include Sūrat al-Kāfirūn and al-Raḥmān.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r6.anchor: ومن مذاهبهم التكرار: إرادة التوكيد والإفهام، كما أن من مذاهبهم الاختصار

IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r7.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r7.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r7.claim: Repeating an oath such as ‘By God, I will not do it’ reinforces resolve; saying ‘By God, I will do it’ with an implied negation is concise.
IBNQUTAYBA-MUSHKIL:v1p149/r7.anchor: والله لا أفعله، ثم والله لا أفعله. إذا أراد التوكيد وحسم الأطماع

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r1.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r1.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r1.claim: Most letter-opened suras immediately mention the Qur'an, book, or revelation; Maryam, al-Ankabut, and al-Rum are exceptions.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r1.anchor: إلا ثلاث سور: {كهيعص} ، {الم (1) أَحَسِبَ النَّاسُ} ، {الم (1) غُلِبَتِ الرُّومُ} - أي: مريم، والعنكبوت، والروم

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r2.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r2.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r2.claim: Bint al-Shati sees an important clue to the disjointed letters in their connection to the Qur'an's rhetorical inimitability, which al-Razi does not pursue.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r2.anchor: لكن الفخر الرازي لم يمض بهذا الملحظ الهام إلى تدبر سر الحرف في الإعجاز البياني

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r3.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r3.speaker: الفخر الرازي
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r3.claim: Al-Razi says letters before Qur'an, book, or revelation alert listeners to attend because the Qur'an is great and its descent and book are weighty.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r3.anchor: أن القرآن عظيم، والإنزال له ثقل، والكتاب له عبء كما قال تعالى: {إِنَّا سَنُلْقِي عَلَيْكَ قَوْلًا ثَقِيلًا}

BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r4.author: ʿĀʾisha ʿAbd al-Raḥmān (Bint al-Shāṭiʾ)
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r4.speaker: author
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r4.claim: Bint al-Shati rejects al-Razi's generalization: heaviness is not unique to letter-opened suras, and al-Kahf mentions the book at its opening without initials.
BINTSHATI-IJAZ:p153/r4.anchor: فثقل القرآن لا تختص به السور المفتتحة بالحروف دون سائر السور الأخرى

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r1.claim: The author initially regarded claims of the Qur'an's inimitability as exaggeration driven by religious zeal, and many stylistic explanations as forced or unscientific.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r1.anchor: وكنت آرى في هذا غلواً ومبالغة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r2.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r2.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r2.claim: After reading widely in language, exegesis, inimitability, and rhetoric, he began accepting the claim, while still considering much writing unconvincing.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r2.anchor: بدأت أميل إلى تصديق هذه المقولة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r3.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r3.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r3.claim: His own comparisons of Qur'anic wording, order, omission, and other features convinced him that every word, letter, and vowel is calculated and that the Qur'an cannot be human speech.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r3.anchor: وجدت تعبيراً فنياً مقصوداً حُسِبَ لكل كلمة فيه حسابُها بل لكل حرف بل لكل حركة

SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r4.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r4.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r4.claim: He offers the book as a guide to some linguistic artistry, admits he may not be free of bias, and invites readers to examine it open-mindedly and patiently rather than accept assertions.
SAMARRAI-ASRAR:r1/r4.anchor: وهذا الكتاب أحسبه من هذا النمط فما هو إلا دليل يشير إلى شيء من مواطن الفن والجمال

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p41/r1.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p41/r1.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p41/r1.claim: Al-Isra is framed by glorification and praise before and after it; the author suggests this hints that the Prophet is being carried to a realm filled with glorification.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p41/r1.anchor: حُفّت السورة كلها بالتسبيح والتحميد قبلها وبعدها ولعلّ في هذا إشارة إلى أنه

SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r7.author: فاضل صالح السامرائي
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r7.speaker: author
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r7.claim: The command to say praise at Al-Isrāʾ's end is answered by the opening of Al-Kahf, which begins with praise for the revelation of the Book.
SAMARRAI-LAMASAT-HALAQAT:p47/r7.anchor: وبعد هذه الآية تبدأ سورة الكهف استجابة لهذا القول

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r1.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r1.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r1.claim: Suyūṭī praises the Qur'an as divinely arranged with profound wisdom, a superb system, eloquent wording, and forceful composition.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r1.anchor: ورتبه بحكمته البالغة أحسن ترتيب ونظمه أعظم نظام بأفصح لفظ وأبلغ تركيب

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r2.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r2.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r2.claim: He describes sustained exploration of the Qur'an's fields and extraction of its sciences, which he collected in works of varied scope.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r2.anchor: فلا أزال أسرح النظر في بساتينه من نوع إلى نوع

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r3.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r3.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r3.claim: Asrār al-Tanzīl investigates Qur'anic styles and wonders, eloquence, figurative expression, and the exposition of its arguments and proofs.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r3.anchor: كتاب أسرار التنزيل الباحث عن أساليبه المبرز أعاجيبه المبين لفصاحة ألفاظه وبلاغة تراكيبه

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r4.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r4.claim: The book examines relationships among sūrahs and the wisdom behind placing each one where it is.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r4.anchor: الأول بيان مناسبات ترتيب سوره وحكمة وضع كل سورة منها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r5.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r5.claim: It argues that each sūrah explains what the preceding sūrah stated concisely.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r5.anchor: الثاني بيان أن كل سورة شارحة لما أجمل في السورة التي قبلها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r6.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r6.claim: It studies how al-Fātiḥah's opening relates to the ending of the preceding sūrah.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r6.anchor: الثالث وجه اعتلاق فاتحة الكتاب بخاتمة التي قبلها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r7.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r7.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r7.claim: It studies the suitability of each sūrah's opening to its purpose, the rhetorical art of a fitting introduction.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r7.anchor: الرابع مناسبة مطلع السورة للمقصد الذي سيقت له وذلك براعة الإستهلال

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r8.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r8.claim: It studies the relationship between the beginnings and endings of sūrahs.

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r9.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r9.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r9.claim: It examines verse order and the connections, interrelation, cohesion, and harmony among verses.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r9.anchor: السادس مناسبات ترتيب آياته واعتلاق بعضها ببعض وارتباطها وتلاحمها وتناسقها

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r10.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r10.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r10.claim: It describes Qur'anic rhetorical styles and variations in address and discourse.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r10.anchor: السابع بيان أساليبه في البلاغة وتنويع خطاباته وسياقاته

SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r11.author: al-Suyūṭī
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r11.speaker: author
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r11.claim: It catalogs rhetorical embellishments and figurative devices, including metaphor, metonymy, insinuation, shifts, double entendre, wordplay, antithesis, comparison, majāz, concision, and expansion.
SUYUTI-TANASUQ:v1p65/r11.anchor: الثامن بيان ما اشتمل عليه من المحسنات البديعية على كثرتها كالإستعارة والكناية والتعريض والإلتفات والتورية والاستخدام واللف والنشر والطباق

NASHR:v1p304#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p304#2/r1.claim: When the pronominal hāʾ precedes a vowel, a preceding fatḥa or ḍamma calls for wāw-linking; a preceding kasra calls for yāʾ-linking, for all readers.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r1.anchor: فالتي قبل متحرك إن تقدمها متحرك وهو فتح أو ضم فالأصل أن توصل بواو لجميع القراء

NASHR:v1p304#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r2.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p304#2/r2.claim: Before a sākin, hāʾ is kasra without a link after kasra or a silent yāʾ, as in ʿabdihi; all readers follow this rule.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r2.anchor: فإن تقدمها كسرة أو ياء ساكنة، فالأصل أن تكسر هاؤه من غير صلة عن الجميع نحو على عبده الكتاب

NASHR:v1p304#2/r3.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r3.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p304#2/r3.claim: Before a sākin, hāʾ is ḍamma without linking after fatḥa, ḍamma, or a consonant other than yāʾ.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r3.anchor: وإن تقدمها فتح أو ضم أو ساكن غير الياء فالأصل ضمه من غير صلة عن كل القراء

NASHR:v1p304#2/r4.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r4.speaker: ابن كثير
NASHR:v1p304#2/r4.claim: When hāʾ follows a sākin before a vowel, Ibn Kathīr links it with yāʾ after yāʾ and with wāw after other consonants; other readers do not link it.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r4.anchor: فإن ابن كثير يصل الهاء بياء في الوصل، وإن كان غير ياء وصلها ابن كثير أيضا بواو

NASHR:v1p304#2/r5.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p304#2/r5.speaker: حفص
NASHR:v1p304#2/r5.claim: Ḥafṣ uses ḍamma without linking in two exceptions, al-Kahf 18:63 and al-Fatḥ 48:10, and links hāʾ in al-Furqān 25:69.
NASHR:v1p304#2/r5.anchor: إلا أن حفصا يضمها في موضعين: وما أنسانيه إلا الشيطان في الكهف، وعاهد عليه الله في الفتح، وافقه حفص على الصلة في حرف واحد

NASHR:v2p465/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p465/r1.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
NASHR:v2p465/r1.claim: ʿAlī ibn al-Ḥusayn relates that the Prophet praised God after completing the Qurʾān, including the words of 18:1; al-Bayhaqī records the report.
NASHR:v2p465/r1.anchor: كان علي بن الحسين - رضي الله عنهما - يذكر عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أنه كان إذا ختم القرآن حمد الله

NASHR:v2p465/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v2p465/r2.speaker: البيهقي
NASHR:v2p465/r2.claim: Al-Bayhaqī describes the Prophetic report on a supplication at the Qurʾān’s completion as disconnected, with a weak chain.
NASHR:v2p465/r2.anchor: وقد روي عن النبي - صلى الله عليه وسلم - في دعاء الختم حديث منقطع بإسناد ضعيف

NASHR:v1p1/r1.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p1/r1.speaker: author
NASHR:v1p1/r1.claim: Because the Qurʾān is the greatest revealed book, its recipient is the best prophet, its community the best, and its bearers, reciters, and teachers the most honored.
NASHR:v1p1/r1.anchor: ولما كان القرآن العظيم أعظم كتاب أنزل، كان المنزل عليه - صلى الله عليه وسلم - أفضل نبي أرسل، وكانت أمته

NASHR:v1p1/r2.author: Ibn al-Jazarī
NASHR:v1p1/r2.speaker: ابن عباس عن النبي
NASHR:v1p1/r2.claim: Ibn ʿAbbās reports the Prophet’s saying that the noblest members of his community are the bearers of the Qurʾān.
NASHR:v1p1/r2.anchor: عن ابن عباس - رضي الله عنهما - قال: قال رسول الله - صلى الله عليه وسلم -: أشراف أمتي حملة القرآن

IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r2.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r2.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r2.claim: The servant is Muhammad; the opening confirms that he is God's Messenger and answers those who questioned his prophethood.
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r2.anchor: يعني محمدا صلى الله عليه وسلم، إنك رسول مني: أي تحقيق لما سألوه عنه من نبوتك

IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r3.author: Ibn Hishām
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r3.speaker: ابن إسحاق
IBNHISHAM:v1p302/r3.claim: The book is upright and moderate, without contradiction.

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r1.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r1.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r1.claim: Ibn Kathir notes that God's book opens with praise in both al-Fatiha and al-Kahf, citing Qur'an 1:2–4 and 18:1–5.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r1.anchor: الحمد لله الذي افتتح كتابه بالحمد فقال: {الحمد لله رب العالمين * الرحمن الرحيم * مالك يوم الدين}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r2.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r2.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r2.claim: Creation begins with praise in Qur'an 6:1, and the account of the final destinies ends with praise in 39:75.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r2.anchor: وافتتح خلقه بالحمد، فقال تعالى: {الحمد لله الذي خلق السماوات والأرض وجعل الظلمات والنور ثم الذين كفروا بربهم يعدلون}

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r3.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r3.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r3.claim: God is praised in this life and the next, in all He has created and will create; Qur'an 28:70 and 34:1 express this comprehensive praise.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r3.anchor: فله الحمد في الأولى والآخرة، أي في جميع ما خلق وما هو خالق، هو المحمود في ذلك كله

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r4.claim: Ibn Kathir cites the prayer “Our Lord, to You belongs praise, filling the heavens and earth and whatever else You will” as an expression of praise without limit.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r4.anchor: كما يقول المصلي: "اللهم ربنا لك الحمد، ملء السماوات وملء الأرض، وملء ما شئت من شيء بعد"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r5.claim: The people of Paradise are inspired to glorify and praise God as naturally as breathing because they witness His immense blessings, power, sovereignty, and unending beneficence; Ibn Kathir links this to Qur'an 10:9–10.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v1p5/r5.anchor: ولهذا يلهم أهل الجنة تسبيحه وتحميده كما يلهمون النفس، أي يسبحونه ويحمدونه عدد أنفاسهم

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r1.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r1.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r1.claim: The Qurʾān is revealed as ordered discourse, sent down in stages according to needs, opened with praise and ended with seeking refuge, and arranged into sūras and verses.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r1.anchor: أنزل القرآن كلاما مؤلفا منظما ونزله بحسب المصالح منجما وجعله بالتحميد مفتتحا

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r2.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r2.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r2.claim: The Qurʾān is Arabic and free of crookedness; it speaks with clear proofs, opens religious and worldly benefits, and confirms earlier heavenly books.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r2.anchor: قرآنا عربيا غير ذي عوج مفتاحا للمنافع الدينية والدنيوية مصداقا لما بين يديه من الكتب السماوية

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r3.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r3.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r3.claim: The Qurʾān is a lasting miracle that defeats every rival across time, place, and language.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r3.anchor: عجزا باقيا دون كل معجز على وجه كل زمان دائرا من بين سائر الكتب على كل لسان في كل مكان

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r4.claim: The eloquent Arabs could not produce anything equal to it, or even approach its shortest sūra; their failure despite intense opposition shows they knew its proof could not be answered.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r4.anchor: فلم يتصد للإتيان بما يوازيه أو يدانيه واحد من فصحائهم ولم ينهض لمقدار أقصر من سورة منه ناهض

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r5.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r5.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r5.claim: The opponents eventually answered the challenge with the sword alone, since they knew the Qurʾān’s argument had overwhelmed them.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r5.anchor: فلم يعارضوا الا السيف وحده على ان السيف القاضب مخراق لاعب إن لم تمض الحجة حده

KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r6.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r6.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r6.claim: The author invokes blessings on Muḥammad, describing him as God’s beloved, protected and supported by wisdom, unlettered, and named in the Torah and Gospel, along with his family, successors, Emigrants, and Helpers.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v1p41/r6.anchor: والصلاة والسلام على خير من اوحى اليه حبيب الله أبي القاسم محمد بن عبد الله

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r1.claim: The Quran is a miracle proving its revelation, protected from alteration, and a proof of the Messenger’s truth; it contains clear and obscure material.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r1.anchor: وخصه بمعجز دل على تنزيله ، ومنع من تبديله ، وبين به صدق رسوله ، وجعل ما استودعه على نوعين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r2.claim: People share in understanding the clear material, while scholars interpret the obscure, so the miracle reaches all and degrees of distinction remain.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r2.anchor: يشترك الناس في علم جلية ويختص العلماء بتأويل خفية حتى يعم الإعجاز ، ثم يحصل التفاضل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r3.claim: The commentator limits this work to obscure interpretation, drawing on transmitted reports and reasoning, collecting earlier and later views, and marking his own conjectures as possibilities.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r3.anchor: جعلت كتابي هذا مقصورا على تأويل ما خفي علمه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r4.claim: He omits what is already apparent from the wording so that the commentary is easier to consult and understand.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r4.anchor: وعدلت عما ظهر معناه من فحواه اكتفاء بفهم قارئه وتصور تالية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r5.claim: He precedes the commentary with foundational chapters that clarify difficult interpretations and hidden evidence.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r5.anchor: وقدمت لتفسيره فصولا ، تكون لعمله أصولا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r6.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r6.claim: The Quran has four names in the Book: Quran, Furqan, Book, and Reminder, supported by citations including this verse.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p21/r6.anchor: سمى الله القرآن في كتابه بأربعة أسماء
